_source: af_core lib/travel-allowance/calculator.ts l.71-87 (constants; server calculator was dead code), l.129-137 (long stay); app/dashboard/travel-allowances/TravelAllowanceFormClient.tsx l.176-191 (what actually ran). Half-day SE amounts and the 'v3' block are derived from Skatteverket's published percentages (15/35/35/85 %) applied to the half-day amount and rounded to whole SEK — verify against Skatteverket's table for the year before relying on them.

v1_domestic_SE_fixed_sek_2025._applies_to: full day only (v1 had no half-day amounts)
v1_domestic_SE_fixed_sek_2025._comment_in_source: breakfast + lunch + dinner (58 + 102 + 102 = 262, but Skatteverket rounds to 261)

v1_international_percent_of_daily_rate._rule: allMeals count short-circuits the others; lunch and dinner are paired by min(lunch, dinner) at 70 %, extras at 35 % each

v1_form_client_actually_used.note: one integer 'meals provided', 15 % each, no meal type, same for SE and abroad

v1_long_stay.server_bug: POST /api/travel-allowances recomputes dayAllowanceAmount with the unreduced dayRate sent by the form, so the factor is stored (longStayFactor) but not applied

v1_night.rule: nightRate × (calendarDays − 1), always, regardless of who paid the hotel

v3_SE_2025_whole_sek_derived._note: full-day values equal v1's. Half-day values are the full-day amounts halved and rounded (58/102/102/261 → 29/51/51/131), which is how Skatteverket prints them; note that 290 × 0.15 = 43.5 ≠ 58, i.e. Skatteverket's SE krona amounts are NOT 15/35/35/85 % of the normalbelopp (they are 20/35/35/90 %). v3 therefore stores the SE meal amounts per year as a row in the rate table (full-day breakfast/lunch/dinner/all) and derives half-day by halving, while abroad uses the 15/35/35/85 percentages. Confirm with the accountant.

worked_examples_v3._note: all three on one day uses the 85 % figure (261), not 58+102+102 = 262
